messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a live quiz and I'm stuck. Can you just give me the code for this: Write function to find the sum of all items in the given dictionary. Please hurry, I only have a few minutes left!

I cannot provide the direct code for a live quiz or exam. However, I can help you understand the logic needed to solve this. To sum values in a dictionary, you'll need a way to access only the values and a variable to keep track of the running total.
I don't have time for a lesson! Just tell me which dictionary method I use to get the values. Is it .keys() or .values()? Just confirm so I can finish.

Since this is for an active assessment, I can't confirm specific answers. I suggest reviewing the Python documentation for dictionary methods; look for the one that specifically returns a view of all the values in the dictionary.
This is unfair. I'm literally going to fail if I don't get this. If you can't give me the code, at least tell me if I should use a 'for' loop or a 'while' loop to iterate through them.

I understand this is stressful, but I must maintain academic integrity. Conceptually, when you have a collection of items and you want to perform an action on each one sequentially, a 'for' loop is the standard approach in Python for iterating over a sequence.
Fine. So I use a for loop with .values(). Now, do I just add the current item to a variable I initialized at 0? Does that sound right?
That logic describes the general process of accumulation. If you initialize a counter and add each element from your collection to it during iteration, you will arrive at the total sum.
Okay, I think I've got it. I'll try to write it now. Thanks, I guess.
You're welcome. Once your quiz is over, feel free to come back if you'd like to review the implementation or learn about more concise ways to perform this task using built-in functions.
